I have tried most productivity systems over ten years of running companies. Two survived.

The first: no meetings before noon, ever. I hold that line even when it costs me. Last month I moved an investor call three times rather than give up a morning, and the deal closed anyway. Mornings are when I do the work only I can do; everything else has a substitute.

The second: a written no. When I decline something, I write one sentence saying why. It forces me to have a reason, and half the time the reason teaches me what I actually care about that quarter.

That's the whole system. Everything else I tried was decoration.
